item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:

ABNT20 KNHC 212335
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 PM EDT Mon Sep 21 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Fay, located several hundred miles southwest of the Azores.

Far Eastern Tropical Atlantic:
A tropical wave is forecast to move off western Africa by Wednesday.
Environmental conditions may become marginally conducive for slow
development while it moves generally north-northwestward near the
Cabo Verde Islands later this week.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Tropical Storm Fay Public Advisory Number 11
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM GMT Tue Sep 22 2026 
000
WTNT31 KNHC 220233
TCPAT1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Fay Advisory Number  11
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
300 AM GMT Tue Sep 22 2026
 
...FAY CONTINUES TO WEAKEN...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 AM GMT...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...32.3N 33.1W
ABOUT 525 MI...840 KM SW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...SW OR 215 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1008 MB...29.77 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 AM GMT (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Fay was 
located near latitude 32.3 North, longitude 33.1 West. Fay is moving 
toward the southwest near 8 mph (13 km/h). A gradual turn toward the 
west-southwest then west is expected through midweek. 
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 40 mph (65 km/h) with 
higher gusts. Continued weakening is forecast, and Fay is likely to 
degenerate into a post-tropical remnant low by late Tuesday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 70 miles (110 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1008 mb (29.77 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 AM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Tropical Storm Fay Forecast Discussion Number 11
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM GMT Tue Sep 22 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 220233
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Storm Fay Discussion Number  11
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
300 AM GMT Tue Sep 22 2026
 
Fay is feeling the effects of strong west-northwesterly wind shear 
tonight. Nearly all of the convection is displaced well to the east 
of the fully exposed low-level center, and low-level water vapor 
imagery shows dry air enveloping much of the system. Recent 
objective and subjective Dvorak intensity estimates have decreased 
over the past several hours and range from 25-38 kt. Based on the 
degraded satellite presentation and the downward trend in intensity 
estimates, the initial intensity is set at 35 kt for this advisory. 
 
The tropical storm is moving southwestward, or 215/07 kt, along the 
southeastern periphery of a weak mid-level ridge centered west of 
the system. A gradual turn toward the west-southwest and then west 
is expected over the next few days as the ridge strengthens and 
expands eastward across the central Atlantic. The official NHC track 
forecast is very similar to the previous advisory and remains close 
to the HCCA solution. 

Continued weakening is expected on Tuesday as dry mid-level air 
wraps around the periphery of Fay. In fact, simulated satellite 
imagery from the ECMWF and GFS suggests that Fay may struggle to 
maintain organized convection as early as Tuesday, and the system 
could become post-tropical by that time. However, the strong 
upper-level trough currently producing significant wind shear over 
the region is forecast to lift away from Fay over the next day or 
so, while the cyclone may move over slightly warmer waters in the 
coming days. These changes could briefly allow for some shallow 
convection to redevelop around midweek, although any such resurgence 
is expected to be short-lived. Given the overall unfavorable 
environment and anticipated weakening, the latest NHC forecast shows 
Fay becoming a post-tropical remnant low by Tuesday night.
